items.text: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director with immediate effect. He resigned on Nov 12 after reports of relationships with two employees and with a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese agent. Chairman Harvey Jones, who had said Huang would not return, now says he is the right leader. The board said it had input from senior levels of the US government and that the return poses no national security risk. Its independent probe into the Megaspeed ties will continue, and it has set up a National Security and Export Control Committee. Trump had pushed publicly for Huang's return and praised the decision on Truth Social; NBC's headline says he spoke to the board directly and indirectly.
items.reporter: Grace O'Donnell, David Hollerith, Ines Ferré
items.notes: NBC's account of Trump's role comes from its headline only; the NBC article could not be read. Reuters copy carried via Lufkin Daily News.

items.text: AP reports bipartisan anger at the reinstatement. Outgoing Senate Banking chair Tim Scott (R) said Huang will testify publicly on Dec 3, followed by an interview with three House committees. Republicans John Cornyn and John Curtis asked what the no-risk finding rested on and which officials weighed in. Incoming Democratic chairs Elizabeth Warren, Robert Garcia, Jim Himes and Ron Wyden promised scrutiny; Garcia said Trump's involvement raises national security and corruption questions. Sen. Ruben Gallego called for a probe of stock trades before the announcement.
items.notes: House interview date conflicts: Axios (Nov 17) said Dec 1; AP now says the week after the Dec 3 Senate hearing.

items.text: The S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17, ending a seven-session losing streak; the Nasdaq gained 6.51% to 24,089.56 and the Dow about 3% to 49,595.31. Nvidia jumped about 31%, and chip and neocloud stocks rallied hard. Energy was the only falling sector as WTI slipped to about $80. The 10-year yield stayed near 4.92-4.94%. The gain recovered a little over half of the previous week's roughly 8.6% S&P fall, which had pushed the index into correction. Nomura's Charlie McElligott attributed much of the move to mechanical buying and short covering (analysis).
items.reporter: Ragini Mathur, Avinash P, Niket Nishant
items.notes: Closing levels from STL.News, an aggregator citing AP/Reuters. Nvidia's gain reported as 31.5% to 32.2%.

items.text: New York Fed President John Williams said inflation remains too high, with risks tilted upward, and that rates are likely to rise over time. Asked about consecutive hikes, he said he was not ruling out any options. He said tech-stock swings would matter only if they hit spending and hiring. Governor Lisa Cook repeated that waiting too long risks falling behind the curve. CME FedWatch showed about 98% odds of a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting; Polymarket about 91%. October PCE inflation is due Wednesday.
items.notes: CNBC article could not be loaded; Williams detail rests on a secondary flash summary. Treat quotes as reported.

items.text: CrowdStrike said in an SEC filing that Zscaler holders will get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, valuing Zscaler at about $43.9 billion. The company says the deal will lift free cash flow per share immediately after closing. It needs regulatory approvals; no timetable was given. Zscaler shares rose about 13-15% and CrowdStrike fell about 10%.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said talks with Canada have progressed and a deal is fairly close, without giving terms or a date. He criticised Canada's decision to admit more Chinese electric vehicles and extend tariff relief to some Chinese steel and aluminium, saying Washington wants to protect North American production in those sectors. No deal had been announced by Monday. PM Mark Carney says Canada wants a deal while diversifying trade.
items.notes: Venue of Greer's remarks not stated. No new US tariff proclamation found for Nov 23.

items.text: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the US blockade and sanctions amount to military aggression and that Iran may use any means of self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter. He called reports of Iranian ships loading oil speculation, and said Hormuz could reopen within two days if Washington lifts the blockade and sanctions. TankerTrackers.com reported one tanker loading Iranian crude by ship-to-ship transfer, which would be the first export since the blockade was reimposed in July. No US interdiction was reported.
items.notes: Accounts conflict: TASS cites Iranian state media calling the 14-tanker convoy reports false; TankerTrackers reports one tanker loading.

items.text: Sitting en banc in Texas AG Ken Paxton's suit, the Fifth Circuit held 9-8 that the PWFA is invalid because it passed in the December 2022 spending package while most House members voted by proxy. The eight dissenters noted no one objected to the quorum at the time. Advocates say workers in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi lose the law's accommodations, and the ruling could invite challenges to other proxy-era laws. The DOJ had defended the law; A Better Balance expects a Supreme Court appeal. Coverage spread on Nov 22-23.
items.notes: Framing differs: Daily Caller (right) treats it as vindicating in-person voting; Yahoo/AP stresses lost worker protections. Majority author not confirmed.

items.text: The FDA approved once-daily giredestrant as monotherapy after surgery for stage I-III ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer at intermediate-to-high risk of recurrence. In the 4,170-patient lidERA trial it cut the risk of invasive recurrence or death by 30% versus standard endocrine therapy. The approval came under Priority Review with required overall-survival follow-up. Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas announced it.
items.notes: No FDA recalls dated Nov 21-24 seen.

items.text: Eleven-term Republican Virginia Foxx conceded after the NC-5 recount left Hubbard's win unchanged. Democrats will hold 11 of North Carolina's 14 House seats.
items.notes: Margin from AP via other outlets; WRAL did not state it.

items.text: According to Axios, summarised by Just Security, Jay Clayton will serve as acting National Cyber Director after Sean Cairncross's departure, pending Senate confirmation of Kirsten Davies. The handover comes amid unexplained federal outages and the NCIC and USDA breaches.
